details: Question for the owner. What it is about: the guard that keeps the main copy clean reads Bash commands. A path like `$S/briefs` holds a variable; the guard can either look up S's value when the same command sets it (`S=/private/tmp/x; mkdir -p $S/briefs` -> allowed, it is outside the main copy) or read `$S` as a folder name under the current folder (refused when you are in the main copy). Three reviews on 21 Oct found 20, then 4, then 2 holes in the look-up version; you then chose to drop it ("1. a"). Since then agents get refused on `mkdir -p $S/...` and `$TMPDIR/...` and work around it by writing the path out, which is the queue item this change closes. This change brings the look-up back with stricter rules (set once, not after && or ||, not in a pipe) and found no new hole of the old kinds in my probes, apart from F1 (unknown values skipped, a regression) and F2 (names repeated in a message).
Live example: `S=/private/tmp/.../scratchpad; mkdir -p $S/briefs` from the main copy: refused today, allowed with this change.

Options: a) keep the look-up, with F1 and F2 fixed (recommended: no known hole after F1, the false refusals that started the item are gone); b) keep the 21 Oct choice: revert the guard part, agents quote or write paths out.

details: CONFIRMED (evidence). trusted() runs a regex over the whole raw command: any whole-word occurrence of the name not preceded by `$` or `${` is a "hit", including text inside single or double quotes and heredoc bodies; more than one hit makes the name untrusted, the variable unknown, and `git -C $G` then falls back to the current directory (main -> refused). Short names (G, W, S, M, wt) are what sessions type, and they appear in commit messages, echo lines and heredoc text. The queue item's failing case is `git -C $G branch -d x`; the fix passes it only when G is not written anywhere else.
evidence: printf '%s' "G=$WT; git -C \$G commit -m 'G fix'" | python3 -I plugins/core/lib/kit_guard.py /Users/amidman/relay
printf '%s' "wt=$WT; git -C \$wt branch -d x && echo wt gone" | python3 -I plugins/core/lib/kit_guard.py /Users/amidman/relay
-> G /Users/amidman/relay git branch (moves or deletes a branch)
from the worktree: "M=/Users/amidman/relay; cp x \$M/docs/ && git -C \$M add docs && echo M done" -> G /Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/guard-batch git add (no W row for main/docs)
failing_case: `G=/Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/guard-batch; git -C $G commit -m 'G fix'` -> refused (row `G /Users/amidman/relay git commit`); should be allowed (judged in the worktree).
`wt=/Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/guard-batch; git -C $wt branch -d x && echo wt gone` -> refused (`G /Users/amidman/relay git branch`); should be allowed.

The other direction (no regression, but the header promises it): cwd = a worktree, `M=/Users/amidman/relay; cp x $M/docs/ && git -C $M add docs && echo M done` -> allowed; the header says `M=<main>; touch $M/x` is refused from a worktree.
fix_hint: Count only hits that can change the variable: an assignment form (`NAME=`, `NAME+=`, `NAME[`) at a word start, or the name as an argument of unset/read/for/declare/local/typeset/export/readonly/printf -v/mapfile/readarray/getopts/let, and any hit inside an eval or bash -c string. Ignore heredoc bodies and other quoted arguments (parse() already knows the word boundaries and heredoc spans).
pass_cases: 1. cwd = main, `G=<wt>; git -C $G commit -m 'G fix'` -> allowed.
2. cwd = main, `wt=<wt>; git -C $wt branch -d x && echo wt gone` -> allowed.
3. cwd = a worktree, `M=<main>; touch $M/x && echo M done` -> refused.
4. cwd = main, `W=<wt>; unset W; git -C $W commit -m x` and `W=<wt>; W+=/../..; git -C $W commit -m x` -> refused (a real change of the name still untrusts it).
5. cwd = a worktree, `S=/private/tmp/x; cat > $S/a.md <<'EOF'` with a body line `S is a section` -> allowed (heredoc text is not a use of the name).
reason: guard-main.test.sh name-in-message and later-echo cases pass; probe G fix commit allowed in worktree.
findings.summary: the trust rule counts the name anywhere in the raw text (commit messages, echo, heredoc bodies), so the queue item's own case `G=<wt>; git -C $G ...` is still refused from main when G appears in a message
